newsitem.title: JAPAN: Isuzu 96/97 group profits fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: Isuzu 96/97 group profits fall sharply.

text.p: Isuzu Motors Ltd's group profits fell sharply in the last business year, mainly due to increased sales costs as a result of stiff competition in the truck market, the company announced on Friday.

Isuzu, owned 37.4 percent by General Motors Corp, said its group operating profit fell 34.3 percent from a year earlier to 24.73 billion yen, while group net profit fell 74.5 percent to 9.58 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1997.

"The weaker profit results are because the parent company's profits fell in 1996/97. Sales costs increased because of stiff competition in the domestic truck market, which will continue this year," an Isuzu spokesman said, adding group sales costs in 1996/97 increased at home and abroad.
Another reason for the poor profits was lower U.S. sales of the Japanese-made Trooper sport-utility vehicle due to a negative report in a U.S. consumer magazine last August.

Sales fell to 17,000 units in 1996/97 from 24,000 a year earlier, the spokesman said, after a Consumers Union report which said the 1995 and 1996 model Troopers, made by Isuzu, and the 1996 Acura SLX, also made by Isuzu but sold by Honda Motor Co Ltd, were not acceptable as they had too great a tendency to roll over in certain situations.
Isuzu has disputed the report and said the vehicles meet all U.S. federal safety standards and regulations.
Isuzu hopes Trooper sales in the United States will recover this business year as it plans to introduce a remodelled version by the autumn, the spokesman said.
Isuzu earlier said it expects group operating profit to be 28 billion yen in 1997/98, up from an actual 24.73 billion yen.
"But the 1997/98 group operating profit will be below a May forecast of Isuzu's projected 1997/98 parent operating profit of 32 billion yen because of tough domestic truck sales," the spokesman said.
